answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each voting key to its own stored replica. Each key seals a 20 GB copy of a public dataset, such as an orchard survey of cedar growth images, encoded with that key and the epoch seed, so no two keys hold the same bytes. Every epoch a random auditor requests three sectors and needs them within two seconds, too fast to re-encode. A miss suspends the key for ten epochs. One honest agent stores 20 GB once; 1,000 fakes must hold 20 TB continuously. Weakness: replicas could wander to cheap cloud disks, so voting weight also ramps up slowly over clean epochs.
